Projects/Projects/open_projects.description: Choose what happens when you open another project while one is already open. This controls whether Suhina asks you each time, keeps both projects open in separate tabs, or replaces the active project. It does not choose what opens when you start Suhina; use At start for that.

options.name: Ask
options.description: Show a choice when opening another project, so you can decide each time.

options.name: New tab
options.description: Open the project in another tab and keep your current project open.

options.name: Replace
options.description: Open the project in place of the active project. If the active project has unsaved changes, Suhina asks how to handle them before replacing it.

Projects/Projects/open_projects.whenToChange: Choose New tab when comparing projects or moving between them. Choose Replace when you prefer working with one active project at a time. Leave Ask selected if your workflow varies.
Projects/Projects/open_projects.summary: Choose whether another project opens in a new tab or replaces the active project.

Projects/Projects/at_start.summary: Choose what opens when Suhina starts without a project file.
Projects/Projects/at_start.description: This controls the first screen when no project is supplied at launch. A template is a saved starting project that Suhina copies into a new, unsaved project. If no start template is chosen or its file is missing, Suhina shows the start panel with an explanation; if there is no last project recorded, it also leaves you on the panel.

options.name: Panel
options.description: Show the start panel with project and template choices. This is the default.

options.name: New
options.description: Create a new blank project.

options.name: Template
options.description: Create a new project from the file chosen in Start template.

options.name: Last
options.description: Request the project most recently opened or saved, rather than make a new project.

Projects/Projects/at_start.whenToChange: Choose Template if you begin most songs with the same instruments and routing. Choose Panel if you usually choose between several projects.

Projects/Projects/projects_folder.summary: Choose the initial save folder for new projects.
Projects/Projects/projects_folder.description: The save dialog starts in this folder for a project that has no file yet. Type a folder path or use Browse. An empty field uses the default folder shown by Suhina. Existing projects keep their files and use their current folder when saving; changing this field does not move them.
Projects/Projects/projects_folder.whenToChange: Set this to your music projects folder so the first save of each new song starts in the right place.

Projects/Projects/templates_folder.summary: Choose where Suhina finds and saves project templates.
Projects/Projects/templates_folder.description: Templates are projects used as reusable starting points. This folder supplies the templates listed under New → From a template and is the destination used by Save as template. Type a path or use Browse; leave the field empty to use the default shown by Suhina. Changing the folder does not move existing templates.
Projects/Projects/templates_folder.whenToChange: Change this when you keep reusable starting projects in a dedicated folder or on another drive.

Projects/Projects/start_template.summary: Choose the template used by the Template startup option.
Projects/Projects/start_template.description: Enter a template file name from Templates folder, or an absolute path to a template, or use Browse to select the file. Suhina creates a new project from it at startup only when At start is Template. This control is hidden for the other startup choices. An empty or missing template leaves the start panel visible with an explanation.
Projects/Projects/start_template.whenToChange: Select your usual recording or songwriting template after setting At start to Template.

Projects/Backups/backup.summary: Choose when changed projects receive recovery copies.
Projects/Backups/backup.description: A backup is a separate project copy, not a replacement for saving your project. Suhina backs up open projects only when they have unsaved changes that are newer than their last backup. Saved projects keep copies in a .backup folder alongside their project file; projects never saved use Suhina’s settings backup folder. After an interrupted session, recovery can offer these copies.

options.name: Before critical operations
options.description: Back up before closing a project or quitting, relinking files, adding files or a plug-in, or deleting a track, when the project needs a backup.

options.name: Every minute
options.description: Check for a changed project to back up every minute.

options.name: Every 5 minutes
options.description: Use a five-minute interval. This is the default.

options.name: Every 10 minutes
options.description: Use a ten-minute interval.

options.name: Every 15 minutes
options.description: Use a fifteen-minute interval.

options.name: Every 30 minutes
options.description: Use a thirty-minute interval.

options.name: Every 60 minutes
options.description: Use a one-hour interval.

options.name: Every 4 hours
options.description: Use a four-hour interval.

options.name: Never
options.description: Do not create automatic recovery copies.

Projects/Backups/backup.whenToChange: Choose Every minute during intensive editing if you want more frequent recovery points. Continue saving normally to keep the main project file current.

Projects/Backups/backup_clean_up.summary: Keep the newest 20 backup copies of each project.
Projects/Backups/backup_clean_up.description: Clean-up removes older recovery copies when backups are written, keeping the newest 20 for each project. It does not delete the main project file. It only has new backups to clean up when the Backups setting permits them.

options.name: On
options.description: Delete older backups beyond the newest 20 for that project. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Do not automatically prune older backup copies.

Projects/Backups/backup_clean_up.whenToChange: Leave this on for a bounded backup history. Turn it off when you deliberately want to retain older recovery versions and will manage the files yourself.

Audio/Status/Now.summary: Inspect the audio device actually running and its timing reports.
Audio/Status/Now.description: This panel reports live audio rather than saving a preference. Output identifies the device currently playing, including fallback to another output. Latency reports the engine-to-speaker delay and underruns: occasions when audio was not supplied in time. Key to sound estimates the current delay for live notes; arming a track makes the engine keep less audio queued ahead. Input now reports the open input, its channel count and input underruns, or says none is open. List devices again refreshes the available hardware list; it does not itself choose another device. With no playing project, live reports may be empty.
Audio/Status/Now.whenToChange: Check this when the selected interface is unplugged, live notes feel late, or playback breaks up. Compare the reports after changing Output settings.

Audio/Output/audio_host,audio_device,aud.summary: Choose audio hardware, its driver, timing settings and recording input.
Audio/Output/audio_host,audio_device,aud.description: Driver selects the audio system used to reach your hardware; the listed drivers depend on the platform and build. Device selects an output on that driver. Default follows the system choice; a missing chosen output can fall back to the default. Sample rate is the number of audio frames per second; choose a listed rate or Device’s own. Buffer size controls the device buffer where supported, including WASAPI exclusive mode; when labelled Engine block it controls Suhina’s rendering chunks, while the operating system or driver keeps its own device buffer. Smaller chunks alone do not guarantee the same reduction in the latency shown under Now. Exclusive mode applies to supported WASAPI devices and reserves the device for Suhina; other applications are then not heard on it. Input independently selects Off, the default input or a named microphone/interface input on the chosen driver. Input is Off initially. Choosing an input supplies audio to tracks configured to use it; it does not itself arm or record a track.

options.name: Driver: Default / listed driver
options.description: Use the default audio system or explicitly select one. WASAPI is Windows’ audio system; ASIO uses an interface’s ASIO driver when available.

options.name: Device: Default / listed output
options.description: Use the driver’s default output or a named output device. The list follows Driver.

options.name: Sample rate: Device’s own / listed Hz value
options.description: Keep the device’s preferred rate or request one of its advertised rates. Hz means frames per second.

options.name: Buffer size / Engine block: Default / listed frames
options.description: Use the default render block or a listed frame count. Read the row’s label and note to see whether this also sets the device buffer.

options.name: Exclusive mode: On / Off
options.description: On requests WASAPI exclusive access where supported. Off uses shared access. It does not switch ASIO between shared and exclusive operation.

options.name: Input: Off / Default / listed input
options.description: Off opens no audio input. Default follows the driver’s default input; a named choice uses that input device.

Audio/Output/audio_host,audio_device,aud.whenToChange: Select your audio interface and input before recording. If key-to-sound delay is distracting, inspect Now and try a supported smaller buffer; if underruns increase, try a larger one.

Audio/Cue/audio_cue_pair,audio_cue_volum.summary: Route previews to the main outputs or a separate headphone pair.
Audio/Cue/audio_cue_pair,audio_cue_volum.description: The cue is a separate listening path for browser and sample-map previews and tracks whose headphone cue button is on. Cue output chooses a stereo pair on the same device as the main mix. A separate pair lets previews play through headphones without reaching the main speakers. Cue volume sets this listening path’s level without changing the main mix. If a saved pair is unavailable, previews play with the main output until that pair is available again. MIDI previews played through a selected track’s instrument follow that track’s routing rather than the separate fallback preview path.

options.name: Same as main (1/2)
options.description: Play previews with the main mix. A track’s cue button adds no separate audible path. This is the default.

options.name: Outputs 3/4, 5/6, …
options.description: Use an available additional stereo pair on the selected device; the main mix stays on 1/2. A separate second audio device cannot be chosen here.

options.name: Cue volume: -12 dB / -6 dB / 0 dB / +6 dB
options.description: Set the cue quieter, unchanged in level, or louder. dB expresses relative level; 0 dB is the default, with no level adjustment. Browser Preview volume also affects sample previews.

Audio/Cue/audio_cue_pair,audio_cue_volum.whenToChange: Choose outputs connected to headphones when auditioning samples during playback. Use Same as main on a two-output device.

Midi/MIDI inputs/midi_input_off.summary: Enable or disable each connected MIDI input port.
Midi/MIDI inputs/midi_input_off.description: MIDI carries notes and controller messages, not microphone audio. Each listed port has its own On/Off control. Enabled ports can feed note-playing tracks according to each track’s input, monitoring and record-ready state. With automatic monitoring, make the intended track record-ready (arm it) to hear its instrument. A port can report Opening or an opening error; On alone does not guarantee it opened successfully. Ports are enabled unless you have switched them off.

options.name: On
options.description: Open this port and make its MIDI available to tracks configured to receive it.

options.name: Off
options.description: Exclude this port from MIDI input without disabling the other ports.

Midi/MIDI inputs/midi_input_off.whenToChange: Turn off a duplicate or unwanted port if one keyboard is sending notes twice, or enable the port of the controller you want to play.

Midi/Arming/auto_arm.summary: Arm the track you select, so a MIDI controller or the audio input plays into it.
Midi/Arming/auto_arm.description: When this is on, selecting a track (clicking its header, or a clip slot in its column) arms it for recording, and the track armed this way before is disarmed again. On a MIDI track, a MIDI keyboard or controller then plays the track's instrument; on an audio track, the track hears its audio input, and a track with no input chosen gets the device's first input, as its arm button gives it. Return tracks, the main track and groups are left as they are, and the arm does not move while a take is recording. A track you armed yourself stays armed when you select another one. Arming is not an edit: it is not undone and not saved with the project. The setting is off unless you turn it on.

options.name: On
options.description: Selecting a MIDI or audio track arms it, and the track armed by the previous selection is disarmed.

options.name: Off
options.description: Selecting a track does not change which tracks are armed; arm tracks with their own buttons.

Midi/Arming/auto_arm.whenToChange: Turn it on when you play a MIDI keyboard or record an input into one track after another and want the arm to follow the track you select. Leave it off when you record several tracks at once or keep particular tracks armed.

Plugins/Folders/Plug-in library.summary: Manage the folders plug-ins are looked for in.
Plugins/Folders/Plug-in library.description: Plug-ins are separately installed instruments and effects. Each folder has a switch controlling whether scans include it, and a format describing which plug-in files to look for. Standard folders can be disabled; added folders can also be removed from the list without deleting files. Enter a path, choose a format and press Add. Disabling a plug-in keeps it in the catalog but removes it from the browser and prevents newly opened projects from loading it. Folder and plug-in changes wait while scanning runs.

options.name: Folder checkbox: On / Off
options.description: Include or skip the folder in subsequent scans. Turning a folder off removes its plug-ins from the catalog after the next scan.

options.name: Both
options.description: Look for CLAP and VST3 files in an added folder.

options.name: VST3
options.description: Look for VST3 files only in that folder.

options.name: CLAP
options.description: Look for CLAP files only in that folder.

options.name: VST2
options.description: Shown as unavailable: VST2 hosting is not implemented yet.

Plugins/Folders/Plug-in library.whenToChange: Add a custom installation folder when a plug-in is missing. Use Manage plug-ins to inspect a loading failure or temporarily disable a problematic plug-in.

Plugins/Editors/plugin_editors.summary: Choose where a plug-in’s own editing interface opens.
Plugins/Editors/plugin_editors.description: A plug-in editor is the instrument or effect’s own graphical controls. Window gives it a separate window above Suhina; Device view embeds it in the selected track’s device panel. Embedded editors are supported on Windows and X11. The Settings panel reports when editors cannot open on the current system; selecting Device view does not add platform support.

options.name: Window
options.description: Open the editor in its own window. This is the default.

options.name: Device view
options.description: Place the editor in the device panel where embedding is supported; elsewhere this choice cannot provide an embedded editor.

Plugins/Editors/plugin_editors.whenToChange: Choose Device view to keep a plug-in’s controls in the track’s effect chain. Choose Window when you want a separate editor window.

Devices/NAM/nam_models_folder.summary: Choose the folder supplying the NAM Amp Modeler model list.
Devices/NAM/nam_models_folder.description: A NAM model is a .nam file containing a captured amplifier, preamp or pedal response. The NAM Amp Modeler uses this folder to list available models in its device panel. Type a folder or use Browse; an empty field uses the default shown in Suhina. Choosing a folder does not itself select or replace the model loaded in an effect.
Devices/NAM/nam_models_folder.whenToChange: Point this at the folder where you store your .nam captures so you can choose them from the Amp Modeler panel.

Devices/NAM/irs_folder.summary: Choose the folder supplying the NAM Cab Loader response list.
Devices/NAM/irs_folder.description: An impulse response, or IR, is a short audio recording of how a speaker cabinet and microphone respond to a brief signal. The NAM Cab Loader lists .wav response files from this folder. Type a folder or use Browse; an empty field uses the default shown in Suhina. Changing the folder does not itself replace the response loaded in an effect.
Devices/NAM/irs_folder.whenToChange: Choose your cabinet-response folder when the Cab Loader list does not show the .wav responses you want.

Devices/Device panels/device_chain.summary: Show a track's instruments and effects side by side below the tracks, or stacked in a side panel.
Devices/Device panels/device_chain.description: A device chain is the collection of instruments and effects on a track. Select a track to see these controls in the detail area, the panel used for devices and clip editing. This setting changes how that panel and its device controls are arranged; it does not reorder the effects or change the sound.

options.name: Row (default)
options.description: Place the detail area below the Session or Arrangement view, with device controls arranged side by side. Use Detail area layout to choose whether this bottom panel also extends underneath the browser.

options.name: Stack
options.description: Place the detail area in a column beside the Session or Arrangement view, with device controls arranged vertically. Detail area layout does not affect this side-panel arrangement.

Devices/Device panels/device_chain.whenToChange: Choose Row when you want to see several effects side by side along the bottom. Choose Stack when you prefer a vertical column of controls beside the tracks.

Devices/Device panels/detail_layout.summary: Let the bottom editing panel extend underneath the browser, or keep the browser full height beside it.
Devices/Device panels/detail_layout.description: The detail area shows the selected track's instruments and effects, or the selected clip's editor. When Device chain is set to Row, this panel sits at the bottom of the window. This setting decides how the bottom panel shares space with the browser, the panel where you find samples, instruments and files. It has no effect while Device chain is set to Stack.

options.name: Beside (default)
options.description: Keep the browser running down to the bottom of the window. The detail area uses the remaining width beside the browser, so it does not extend underneath it.

options.name: Full width
options.description: Extend the detail area across the bottom of the whole window, including the space underneath the browser. The browser becomes shorter to leave room for this wider editing panel.

Devices/Device panels/detail_layout.whenToChange: Choose Full width if the piano roll or a long row of effects needs more horizontal room. Choose Beside if you want to keep a taller browser visible while editing. Set Device chain to Row first if you currently use Stack.

Importing/Dropping files/drop_files.summary: Choose how several dropped files are distributed across tracks.
Importing/Dropping files/drop_files.description: When importing several files together, choose whether they share one track or each gets a track. Holding Ctrl while dropping reverses the selected behavior for that drop. This concerns multi-file placement; it does not rearrange files already in the project. On macOS the command modifier is Cmd.

options.name: One track
options.description: Place the files on one track; Ctrl while dropping uses separate tracks. This is the default.

options.name: One each
options.description: Give the files separate tracks; Ctrl while dropping places them on one track.

Importing/Dropping files/drop_files.whenToChange: Choose One each when importing separate song parts that should have their own mixer channels.

Importing/Dropping files/warp_mode.summary: Choose how newly imported samples follow the project tempo.
Importing/Dropping files/warp_mode.description: Warping maps a sample’s recorded timing to musical beats so it can follow the project tempo. This setting supplies the stretch mode for dropped samples whose tempo is known. A sample without a known tempo is not automatically warped. It does not change the modes of existing clips. Currently Rhythmic, Tonal, Texture, Smooth and High quality all use the same pitch-preserving stretch algorithm; their names do not give different sound quality yet. Unsupported files or extreme stretch ratios can fall back to Re-pitch.

options.name: Rhythmic
options.description: Keep pitch while fitting the sample to the project tempo. This is the default.

options.name: Tonal
options.description: Use the same current pitch-preserving algorithm as Rhythmic, while storing Tonal as the clip’s intended mode.

options.name: Texture
options.description: Use the same current pitch-preserving algorithm, while storing Texture as the intended mode.

options.name: Smooth
options.description: Use the same current pitch-preserving algorithm, while storing Smooth as the intended mode.

options.name: High quality
options.description: Use the same current pitch-preserving algorithm; this choice does not currently enable a different quality level.

options.name: Re-pitch
options.description: Read audio faster or slower to fit the tempo: faster is higher in pitch, slower is lower. Clip transpose does not apply in this mode.

Importing/Dropping files/warp_mode.whenToChange: Choose Re-pitch if you want speed and pitch to change together. Keep a pitch-preserving choice when a loop should follow your song tempo without changing its key.

Arrangement/Clip editing/sample_stacking.summary: Choose whether overlapping audio clips play together or replace covered material.
Arrangement/Clip editing/sample_stacking.description: Stacking keeps overlapping audio clips on one Arrangement track and lets them all play. With stacking off, placing a clip over another removes the covered part: a fully covered clip is removed, and a partly covered clip is shortened or split. Overlapping clips are shown in sub-rows so they remain reachable. This preference is used for moves and related clip placement actions, not as a command to remove existing overlaps. For a file drop, the current implementation requests stacking if either audio or MIDI stacking is enabled.

options.name: On
options.description: Keep overlapping audio clips and play them together.

options.name: Off
options.description: Replace the covered portion when placing clips. This is the default.

Arrangement/Clip editing/sample_stacking.whenToChange: Turn this on to layer audio clips on one track. Keep it off when a clip you place should replace the material it covers.

Arrangement/Clip editing/midi_stacking.summary: Choose whether overlapping MIDI clips play together or replace covered material.
Arrangement/Clip editing/midi_stacking.description: Stacking keeps overlapping MIDI clips on one Arrangement track and lets them all play. With stacking off, placing a clip over another removes the covered part: a fully covered clip is removed, and a partly covered clip is shortened or split. Overlapping clips are shown in sub-rows so they remain reachable. This preference is used for moves and related clip placement actions, not as a command to remove existing overlaps. For a file drop, the current implementation requests stacking if either audio or MIDI stacking is enabled.

options.name: On
options.description: Keep overlapping MIDI clips and play them together.

options.name: Off
options.description: Replace the covered portion when placing clips. This is the default.

Arrangement/Clip editing/midi_stacking.whenToChange: Turn this on to layer note-playing clips on one track. Keep it off when a clip you place should replace the material it covers.

Arrangement/Clip editing/double_click_cl.summary: Create an empty clip by double-clicking an empty slot or lane.
Arrangement/Clip editing/double_click_cl.description: This enables double-click creation on an empty Session slot or empty Arrangement lane position of a track that can hold clips. The clip matches the track’s kind: MIDI on a note-playing track, audio on an audio track. An empty audio clip is silent until it has audio content. This is separate from the piano roll’s double-click settings for creating notes.

options.name: On
options.description: Double-click empty clip space to create a clip. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Do not create an empty clip with that double-click gesture.

Arrangement/Clip editing/double_click_cl.whenToChange: Turn this off if you often create clips accidentally while navigating empty space.

Arrangement/Clip editing/menu_name_field.summary: Choose whether a clip’s context menu includes an editable name field.
Arrangement/Clip editing/menu_name_field.description: The clip context menu is the menu opened by right-clicking a clip. With this enabled, it contains a name field for editing the clip name. With it disabled, Rename opens name editing on the clip instead. This changes where you type a name, not the clip’s audio or notes.

options.name: On
options.description: Show an editable name field in the clip menu.

options.name: Off
options.description: Use Rename, or Ctrl+R, to edit the clip label. This is the default.

Arrangement/Clip editing/menu_name_field.whenToChange: Enable it if you prefer typing a name inside the right-click menu rather than editing the label on the clip.

Arrangement/Clip editing/clip_drag.summary: Choose which part of an Arrangement clip moves it and which selects time.
Arrangement/Clip editing/clip_drag.description: A clip can have a name bar above its waveform or note preview. This preference divides the clip into movement and time-selection regions. Ctrl+drag selects time over clips overrides that division when enabled. Very short clip rows without room for a name bar use upper and lower regions. Clicking a clip body can set the play start at the clicked position instead of choosing the whole clip’s span.

options.name: Name bar
options.description: Drag the name bar to move the clip and drag the body to select time. This is the default.

options.name: Mirror
options.description: Drag the lower half to move the clip and the upper half to select time.

Arrangement/Clip editing/clip_drag.whenToChange: Choose Name bar for a clear move handle above the clip content. Choose Mirror if you prefer moving clips from their lower half.

Arrangement/Time and play/time_select.summary: Use Ctrl-drag for time selection instead of dividing clips into drag regions.
Arrangement/Time and play/time_select.description: A time selection is a span of the timeline across one or more tracks; editing can act on material inside that span. This setting changes how you paint that selection over Arrangement clips and lanes. When enabled, an ordinary clip drag moves it and Ctrl-drag selects time; Shift-drag is then the copy gesture. When disabled, Moving a clip determines the clip’s move and selection regions, and Ctrl-drag copies clips. A ruler drag selects time in either mode. Ctrl is Cmd on macOS.

options.name: On
options.description: Ctrl-drag selects time over clips; plain clip dragging moves, and Shift-drag copies.

options.name: Off
options.description: Use clip regions for time selection and movement, as set by Moving a clip. This is the default.

Arrangement/Time and play/time_select.whenToChange: Enable this when you prefer using the whole clip as a move handle and holding a modifier to select time.

Arrangement/Time and play/play_from_sele.summary: Move the play start marker to newly selected whole clips while stopped.
Arrangement/Time and play/play_from_sele.description: The play start marker is the timeline position used by marker-based playback. With this enabled, changing the whole-clip selection while stopped moves that marker to the earliest selected clip’s start. It does not move the marker during playback. A click in a clip body still sets the position where you clicked; clips on a track edited by an ARA audio editor also keep their own position behavior. Transport → Play from separately chooses whether Play uses the marker or the selected clip.

options.name: On
options.description: Move the marker to the first selected whole clip when the selection changes while stopped. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Do not move the marker merely because whole clips were selected.

Arrangement/Time and play/play_from_sele.whenToChange: Turn this off if whole-clip selection should leave a carefully placed play start marker alone, and set Transport → Play from to Marker when that is the position Play should use.

Arrangement/Time and play/play_start.summary: Choose the starting position used by Play and the play/stop shortcut.
Arrangement/Time and play/play_start.description: The play start marker marks the timeline position from which playback can begin. Selected clip instead starts from a whole clip selected in the Arrangement. With no suitable whole-clip selection, Play uses the marker. Clicking a clip body uses the clicked position, and clips on an ARA audio-editor track also use the position set by that editor or a click. Arrangement → Play from the selected clip separately controls whether changing selection moves the marker.

options.name: Marker
options.description: Start from the current play start marker.

options.name: Selected clip
options.description: Start at the selected whole Arrangement clip where applicable, otherwise use the marker. This is the default.

Arrangement/Time and play/play_start.whenToChange: Choose Marker to audition from a fixed point while changing the clip selection. Also turn off Arrangement → Play from the selected clip if selection should leave that marker in place.

Arrangement/Time and play/stop.summary: Choose whether Stop returns to the play start marker or stays at the stopped position.
Arrangement/Time and play/stop.description: The playhead shows the current playback position. Marker returns it to the play start marker when you stop. Stay stops at the current position and moves the start marker there. Pressing Stop again while already stopped returns to the song’s beginning. This sets stop behavior; Play from separately determines how the next Play action chooses its start.

options.name: Marker
options.description: Return to the play start marker on stopping. This is the default.

options.name: Stay
options.description: Keep the stopped position and move the start marker there.

Arrangement/Time and play/stop.whenToChange: Choose Marker to rehear a phrase from the same point. Choose Stay when you want to continue from where you stopped.

Arrangement/View/clip_grid.summary: Show the Arrangement beat grid through clip bodies.
Arrangement/View/clip_grid.description: The grid marks musical time with vertical beat and bar lines. Enabling this draws faint lines through clip bodies as well as the empty timeline, making timing easier to compare with waveforms and notes. It changes drawing only; disabling the lines inside clips does not disable snapping.

options.name: On
options.description: Draw grid lines inside clips. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Leave clip bodies without those grid lines; other grid behavior stays available.

Arrangement/View/clip_grid.whenToChange: Turn this off for less visual detail inside clips, or on when aligning visible transients and notes to beats.

Arrangement/View/waveform_zoom.summary: Enlarge the drawn waveforms in Arrangement audio clips without changing volume.
Arrangement/View/waveform_zoom.description: A waveform shows audio level over time. Waveform zoom magnifies its vertical drawing across the Arrangement’s audio clips, helping quiet detail show up. It does not change the audio, gain or time scale. The waveform slider near the Arrangement ruler and Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down adjust the same preference and can provide values beyond the four buttons here.

options.description: Draw at normal waveform size. This is the default.
Draw waveform amplitudes twice as large.
Draw waveform amplitudes four times as large.
Draw waveform amplitudes eight times as large.

Arrangement/View/waveform_zoom.whenToChange: Increase this when a quiet recording looks almost flat and you want to see its timing clearly.

Arrangement/Tracks/new_track_colour.summary: Give new tracks successive palette colors or one fixed palette color.
Arrangement/Tracks/new_track_colour.description: The palette is the theme’s set of track colors. This chooses how a new track gets its initial color. Existing tracks retain their stored colors when the preference changes or tracks are reordered. You can still set a track’s color individually.

options.name: Alternating
options.description: Choose a palette color by the new track’s position. This is the default.

options.name: Fixed
options.description: Give each new track the palette’s first color.

Arrangement/Tracks/new_track_colour.whenToChange: Choose Alternating to distinguish adjacent tracks quickly, or Fixed when you prefer assigning your own colors after creation.

Arrangement/Tracks/track_headers.summary: Place Arrangement track names and controls on the left or right of the timeline.
Arrangement/Tracks/track_headers.description: Track headers contain each track’s name and controls. This moves their column to the selected edge of the Arrangement timeline. It does not reorder tracks, move the browser, or change the Session view’s columns. Browser side is a separate preference.

options.name: Left
options.description: Show the header column on the left of the Arrangement lanes.

options.name: Right
options.description: Show the header column on the right. This is the default.

Arrangement/Tracks/track_headers.whenToChange: Choose the side that keeps track controls closest to where you usually work on the timeline.

Arrangement/Tracks/arrangement_returns.summary: Show or hide the Arrangement rows for return tracks.
Arrangement/Tracks/arrangement_returns.description: Return tracks receive sound sent from other channels, often for shared effects. This preference hides or shows their rows at the bottom of the Arrangement. Hiding is visual: it does not remove return tracks or mute their audio. The Hide returns / Show returns button near the ruler changes the same preference; the main output row remains.

options.name: Shown
options.description: Include return rows at the bottom. This is the default.

options.name: Hidden
options.description: Leave return rows out of the Arrangement display.

Arrangement/Tracks/arrangement_returns.whenToChange: Hide returns to make more room for ordinary tracks when you are not editing return effects or automation.

Arrangement/Advanced/stretch_alt_drag.summary: Enable pitch-preserving audio stretching with Ctrl+Alt at a clip edge.
Arrangement/Advanced/stretch_alt_drag.description: Time-stretching changes an audio clip’s duration while aiming to retain its pitch. With this enabled, hold Ctrl+Alt while dragging an Arrangement audio clip’s left or right edge to stretch its content to the new span. Suhina adjusts the timing markers and gives shared content a separate copy where necessary. With it disabled, the edge uses normal trimming behavior. Alt alone allows free edge positioning; it is not the stretch gesture. On macOS use Cmd+Option. MIDI clip edges are not affected.

options.name: On
options.description: Ctrl+Alt-drag an audio edge to stretch the content. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Do not use the edge gesture to stretch audio; edge dragging trims the clip.

Arrangement/Advanced/stretch_alt_drag.whenToChange: Enable it to fit a recorded phrase to a different duration by dragging its edge.

Arrangement/Advanced/rename_selected_cli.summary: Apply the name typed after Ctrl+R to every selected Arrangement clip.
Arrangement/Advanced/rename_selected_cli.description: With multiple Arrangement clips selected, this makes the rename action apply the same typed name to all of them as one undoable edit. With it off, renaming targets the last clicked clip. On macOS the default shortcut uses Cmd+R. This is about clip names, not track names.

options.name: On
options.description: Rename all selected Arrangement clips together. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Rename only the clip clicked last.

Arrangement/Advanced/rename_selected_cli.whenToChange: Keep this on when naming several parts of one phrase together. Turn it off if a multi-selection should not rename the other clips.

Session/Launching/select_on_launch.summary: Select a Session clip when its launch control is pressed.
Session/Launching/select_on_launch.description: The Session view is the grid used to launch clips independently of the Arrangement timeline. With this enabled, launching a clip with its slot’s launch control also selects the clip and its track, so the detail area follows that clip. With it off, launch playback can change while you keep editing the previously selected clip. Clicking the clip name still selects it without launching.

options.name: On
options.description: Select the clip when launching it. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Keep the existing selection when launching from the slot’s launch control.

Session/Launching/select_on_launch.whenToChange: Turn this off when performing clip launches while keeping another clip open for editing.

Session/Mixer/mixer_controls.summary: Show track volume and pan as value fields or knobs.
Session/Mixer/mixer_controls.description: Volume sets a track’s level and pan sets its left/right balance. This changes how their controls are drawn, including the Arrangement track headers, without changing the values or sound. Both styles support dragging. Use Ctrl plus the mouse wheel over a value to adjust it instead of scrolling; Ctrl is Cmd on macOS and adding Shift makes the adjustment finer.

options.name: Field
options.description: Show volume as a bar field and pan as a centered field. This is the default.

options.name: Knob
options.description: Show a small rotary control with its numerical value.

Session/Mixer/mixer_controls.whenToChange: Choose Knob if a rotary indicator is easier for you to read, or Field for compact level and balance bars.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_top.summary: Choose what remains visible when the clip editor is pulled to the top.
ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_top.description: The piano roll is the MIDI note editor in the detail area. Dragging its top divider high enough in the Arrangement expands the editor to the top; this also applies to the audio editor supplied by an ARA plug-in. This preference decides whether the edited track’s timeline remains visible. It has no effect on that gesture when Device chain is Stack, because the detail area is then a side column rather than a bottom panel.

options.name: Edited track
options.description: Keep the Arrangement ruler and edited track’s lane above the editor, hiding the other tracks and returns. This is the default.

options.name: Whole window
options.description: Let the editor fill the area below the control bar.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_top.whenToChange: Choose Edited track when you need to see the clip’s place in the song while editing; choose Whole window for the most editor space.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_grid.summary: Give the piano roll its own timing grid or link it to the control bar.
ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_grid.description: A timing grid draws beat divisions and supplies the steps that edited notes snap to. The control bar’s value also controls Arrangement placement and clip-launch timing. Linking the piano roll makes its menu and grid shortcuts change that shared value too. The shared control bar cannot represent adaptive grids or a 1/32 triplet, so those choices are unavailable while linked. This chooses the grid source, not the notes’ timing: existing notes are not automatically moved.

options.name: Its own
options.description: Keep the piano roll’s independent grid and its full menu, initially a snapping 1/16 grid. This is the default.

options.name: Control bar
options.description: Follow and edit the control bar’s grid. Unsupported grid choices are disabled; turning snapping off sets the shared value to none.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_grid.whenToChange: Use Its own for detailed note editing without changing Arrangement snapping or launch timing. Use Control bar when you want a shared grid.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_toolbar.summary: Scale the piano roll toolbar without enlarging the rest of the editor.
ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_toolbar.description: This scales the toolbar’s height, button boxes, gaps and icon strokes together. It gives the note-editing tools larger targets without changing the notes, time ruler or grid size. Appearance → Zoom separately scales the whole interface.

options.name: Normal
options.description: Draw the toolbar at its base size, 100 percent.

options.name: Large
options.description: Scale the toolbar to 125 percent. This is the default.

options.name: Larger
options.description: Scale the toolbar to 150 percent.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/piano_roll_toolbar.whenToChange: Choose Larger when the tool buttons are hard to identify or click; choose Normal to leave more vertical room for notes.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/notes_replace.summary: Replace a note only when a moved note lands on the same pitch and start.
ClipEditor/Piano roll/notes_replace.description: In the piano roll, the grid where MIDI notes are edited, moving a note can land it on an existing note with the same pitch and start time. With replacement on, the existing note is removed. Merely overlapping part of another note does not meet that condition. This preference applies to moves; copying by dragging uses the separate duplicate action.

options.name: On
options.description: Replace the existing note at the same pitch and start. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Keep both notes when a move lands them at the same pitch and start.

ClipEditor/Piano roll/notes_replace.whenToChange: Keep this on when rearranging a melody and you want one note at each start and pitch. Turn it off to retain coincident notes.

Browser/Browser/browser_side.summary: Place the file and instrument browser at the left or right edge of the window.
Browser/Browser/browser_side.description: The browser is the panel used to find samples, MIDI files, instruments, effects and projects. This places that panel on the selected side of the main Session or Arrangement view. It does not choose the side of Arrangement track headers. The preference becomes visible when the browser is shown.

options.name: Left
options.description: Place the browser on the left. This is the default.

options.name: Right
options.description: Place the browser on the right.

Browser/Browser/browser_side.whenToChange: Move the browser to the side that makes dragging files into your tracks most comfortable.

Browser/Browser/browser_recent.summary: Show Recent’s item types in the sidebar or as buttons above the browser list.
Browser/Browser/browser_recent.description: Recent contains recently used items grouped by type, such as Projects, Samples and MIDI. This changes where you choose those types. It does not change what counts as recently used or turn the Library categories into recent-only lists.

options.name: Indented
options.description: List recent types underneath Recent in the browser sidebar. This is the default.

options.name: Chips
options.description: Show type buttons above the results while Recent is selected.

Browser/Browser/browser_recent.whenToChange: Choose Chips to shorten the sidebar, or Indented to keep each recent type directly accessible in the sidebar.

Browser/Previews/preview_autoplay.summary: Preview a browser sample or MIDI file when you select it.
Browser/Previews/preview_autoplay.description: A preview lets you hear a file before adding it to the project. Auto-play starts it when its browser row is selected. With Auto-play off, use the preview play control or click the preview waveform instead. Previews play at the file’s own timing rather than synchronizing to the song. Sample-map hover preview has its own setting. A MIDI preview can use the selected track’s instrument, or a fallback instrument if no suitable track instrument is available.

options.name: On
options.description: Start a preview when a sample or MIDI file is selected. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Selection alone does not start the file preview.

Browser/Previews/preview_autoplay.whenToChange: Turn this off when you want to browse silently and start only the previews you explicitly choose.

Browser/Previews/preview_volume.summary: Set the level used for browser and sample-map previews.
Browser/Previews/preview_volume.description: This is a relative level adjustment in decibels (dB): negative values make previews quieter and 0 dB adds no reduction. It does not change the gain of files imported as clips. The sample map’s Volume control shares this preference. Audio → Cue controls where sample previews are heard and applies its own cue volume too. A MIDI file preview using a track’s instrument follows that track’s signal path.

options.name: -18 dB
options.description: Apply the largest reduction offered by these buttons.

options.name: -12 dB
options.description: Apply a 12 dB reduction.

options.name: -6 dB
options.description: Apply a 6 dB reduction. This is the default.

options.name: 0 dB
options.description: Apply no preview-level reduction; the source level and cue level still matter.

Browser/Previews/preview_volume.whenToChange: Choose a quieter level if auditioning samples is too loud beside your playing project.

Browser/Sample map/map_layout.summary: Arrange similar-sounding samples as a free cloud or a grid.
Browser/Sample map/map_layout.description: The sample map places analyzed samples near other samples with similar sound characteristics. Cloud keeps their free positions; Grid assigns each sample its own cell while trying to preserve neighboring relationships. This changes the map’s display, not the samples or their place in your project. The Cloud / Grid switch on the map changes the same preference.

options.name: Cloud
options.description: Draw sample points at their computed positions. This is the default.

options.name: Grid
options.description: Snap the layout to separate cells so individual samples do not occupy the same cell.

Browser/Sample map/map_layout.whenToChange: Choose Grid when dense clusters make individual samples hard to point at. Choose Cloud to explore the free similarity layout.

Browser/Sample map/map_hover_preview.summary: Hear samples by pointing at them on the sample map.
Browser/Sample map/map_hover_preview.description: Hover means placing the pointer over a sample point without clicking. With this enabled, hovering a new sample starts its preview. It uses the shared preview level and cue routing. This is independent of browser list Auto-play; turning one off does not turn the other off.

options.name: On
options.description: Preview samples as the pointer reaches them. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Do not start a preview merely by hovering a sample.

Browser/Sample map/map_hover_preview.whenToChange: Turn it off if moving the pointer across the map triggers unwanted previews; keep it on to browse by ear.

Browser/Sample map/map_max_seconds.summary: Limit the sample map to files no longer than the chosen duration.
Browser/Sample map/map_max_seconds.description: The sample map is intended for short sounds and loops. Samples exceeding this duration are omitted from the map, but their files remain in the library and can still be found in the normal browser. Changing the limit uses stored duration information and does not require analyzing the audio again. The map’s status reports samples left out for being too long.

options.name: 5 s
options.description: Show samples up to five seconds long.

options.name: 10 s
options.description: Show samples up to ten seconds long. This is the default.

options.name: 30 s
options.description: Include samples up to thirty seconds long.

options.name: 60 s
options.description: Include samples up to one minute long.

Browser/Sample map/map_max_seconds.whenToChange: Raise the limit when a wanted loop is absent because of its length, or lower it to focus on shorter sounds.

Browser/Tags/Tag limit.summary: Set the maximum number of color tags in the browser library.
Browser/Tags/Tag limit.description: A color tag is a named label you assign to library items for filtering and organization. This limits the total number of distinct tags, not the number of files in your library. It is stored with browser library data rather than as a key in settings.txt. Suhina refuses to lower the limit below the number of tags already present; remove unused tags first if needed.

options.description: Allow up to 64 distinct tags. This is the default.
Allow up to 128 tags.
Allow up to 256 tags.
Allow up to 1024 tags.

Browser/Tags/Tag limit.whenToChange: Raise this when you have reached the tag limit and need additional labels for your library.

Keys/Mouse and key behaviour/keymap.json.summary: Choose a keyboard preset or rebind individual actions.
Keys/Mouse and key behaviour/keymap.json.description: This panel lists actions, their assigned keys and controls to Change or Clear them. Change captures the next key with its modifiers; Escape cancels capture. Clear removes an action’s binding. Filter shortcuts searches action names, groups and keys, and conflicts are displayed when one key triggers several actions. Choosing a preset resets keyboard bindings to defaults and applies that preset’s piano-roll workflow behaviors. Editing a workflow choice makes the mode Custom. Reset all currently resets the entire keymap to its default Select-first state. Keys and workflow preferences are saved in keymap.json. Ctrl means Cmd on macOS; Alt means Option.

options.name: Select-first
options.description: Use selection-oriented gestures and Ctrl+D to duplicate. This is the default preset.

options.name: Draw-first
options.description: Use Ctrl+B to duplicate and Ctrl+Shift+B for the browser; right-click deletes notes in Draw and Paint.

options.name: Mouse-first
options.description: Click to draw in Select, right-click to delete, Shift+right-drag to split, and Alt+right to play from the pointer; duplicate remains Ctrl+D.

options.name: Custom
options.description: Keep a mixture of individual workflow choices rather than fill in a preset’s behaviors.

Keys/Mouse and key behaviour/keymap.json.whenToChange: Rebind an action when its default key is awkward on your keyboard, then check for conflicts. Choose a preset when you want a consistent set of note-editing habits.

Keys/Shortcuts/keymap.json.summary: Choose a keyboard preset or rebind individual actions.
Keys/Shortcuts/keymap.json.description: This panel lists actions, their assigned keys and controls to Change or Clear them. Change captures the next key with its modifiers; Escape cancels capture. Clear removes an action’s binding. Filter shortcuts searches action names, groups and keys, and conflicts are displayed when one key triggers several actions. Choosing a preset resets keyboard bindings to defaults and applies that preset’s piano-roll workflow behaviors. Editing a workflow choice makes the mode Custom. Reset all currently resets the entire keymap to its default Select-first state. Keys and workflow preferences are saved in keymap.json. Ctrl means Cmd on macOS; Alt means Option.

options.name: Select-first
options.description: Use selection-oriented gestures and Ctrl+D to duplicate. This is the default preset.

options.name: Draw-first
options.description: Use Ctrl+B to duplicate and Ctrl+Shift+B for the browser; right-click deletes notes in Draw and Paint.

options.name: Mouse-first
options.description: Click to draw in Select, right-click to delete, Shift+right-drag to split, and Alt+right to play from the pointer; duplicate remains Ctrl+D.

options.name: Custom
options.description: Keep a mixture of individual workflow choices rather than fill in a preset’s behaviors.

Keys/Shortcuts/keymap.json.whenToChange: Rebind an action when its default key is awkward on your keyboard, then check for conflicts. Choose a preset when you want a consistent set of note-editing habits.

Appearance/Window/zoom.summary: Scale all interface text, panels and controls together.
Appearance/Window/zoom.description: Window zoom changes the drawing size of the whole interface from 50 to 200 percent. Use the minus and plus controls to change it in ten-percentage-point steps; click the value to return to 100 percent. Ctrl+Plus or Ctrl+Equals, Ctrl+Minus and Ctrl+0 provide the same actions; use Cmd on macOS. This is separate from zooming time in the Arrangement or piano roll.
Appearance/Window/zoom.whenToChange: Increase it when interface text and controls feel too small, or decrease it to show more controls in the available window.

Appearance/Window/animations.summary: Enable or disable interface fades, slides and animated state changes.
Appearance/Window/animations.description: This governs Suhina’s interface motion. With animations off, controls go straight to their final visual states instead of interpolating through a transition. It does not change musical timing, audio playback or the saved project. It is an application preference; it does not control animations on this website.

options.name: On
options.description: Animate interface state changes. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Show the final visual state immediately.

Appearance/Window/animations.whenToChange: Turn this off if interface movement distracts you or you prefer immediate visual changes.

Appearance/Waveforms/waveform_scale.summary: Draw waveform levels linearly or emphasize quiet details with a decibel scale.
Appearance/Waveforms/waveform_scale.description: A waveform is the visible shape of an audio signal over time. Linear drawing makes its height proportional to amplitude, so very quiet passages can look almost flat. The dB scale spreads out quieter levels so those details are easier to see. It affects waveform drawings in clips, browser previews and the sample map; it does not amplify or alter the audio.

options.name: Linear
options.description: Draw amplitude proportionally. This is the default.

options.name: dB
options.description: Use a decibel-based display to make quieter waveform details more visible.

Appearance/Waveforms/waveform_scale.whenToChange: Choose dB when quiet parts are difficult to inspect, and Linear when you want a direct amplitude picture.

Appearance/Advanced/renderer.summary: Choose the graphics system used to draw Suhina after its next start.
Appearance/Advanced/renderer.description: The renderer draws the application window and controls. GPU uses Suhina’s wgpu graphics path; OpenGL uses its OpenGL path. This preference takes effect on the next application start rather than changing the running window. It does not change the audio engine. A command-line renderer choice can override the saved preference for a launch.

options.name: GPU
options.description: Use the wgpu renderer, backed by the platform’s graphics API. This is the default.

options.name: OpenGL
options.description: Use the OpenGL renderer on the next start.

Appearance/Advanced/renderer.whenToChange: Try the other renderer when drawing or resizing the interface is problematic on your system, then apply it at your next planned restart.

Theme/Theme/theme.summary: Select a theme and edit or manage its interface colors.
Theme/Theme/theme.description: A theme is a set of interface colors. Click a theme in the list to use it. Colours lists editable swatches with their purpose and color value; changing a built-in theme’s color first makes a personal copy. A personal theme can be renamed using its name field. Duplicate creates an editable copy; Reload reads theme files again; Open folder shows their location; Back up creates a zip of the theme files; Export template creates a starter theme and format instructions. Dropping a theme file or a zip of themes onto Suhina adds it. These controls affect appearance rather than audio or musical project data.
Theme/Theme/theme.whenToChange: Pick a theme that is comfortable to read, then duplicate it before tailoring colors for your workspace.

Agents/Agents/agents.summary: Allow an attached AI agent to request access to open projects.
Agents/Agents/agents.description: An agent is an external tool that can inspect and edit a project through Suhina’s command interface. Turning this on enables attachment with suhina-cli mcp --attach. Each connection still requires your approval in Suhina. Approved changes appear in the open projects and project edits can be undone. Turning the setting off disconnects attached agents.

options.name: On
options.description: Allow agents to request a connection; this does not approve a connection automatically.

options.name: Off
options.description: Refuse agent attachment and disconnect existing agents. This is the default.

Agents/Agents/agents.whenToChange: Turn this on when you want an assistant to work in the project you are viewing, then approve the intended connection in Suhina.

Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_project.description: Allow attached agents to write in the folder of the project they act on, including its subfolders. This is on by default. Turn it off to require an explicitly added folder for writes. An unsaved project has no project folder. This does not restrict exports you choose yourself in File > Export.

options.name: On
options.description: Allow writes in the project's folder and its subfolders.

options.name: Off
options.description: Allow writes only in explicitly added folders.

Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_project.whenToChange: Turn this off when agents should write only to a separate export folder.

Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_write_f.description: Choose the folders where attached agents may save projects and export audio. Add folder opens the system folder picker; Remove revokes that folder's grant. Each grant includes subfolders and is saved across restarts. Missing folders grant no access. Agents cannot change these permissions. Revocation applies to new operations and exports still gathering plug-in state, but does not cancel a render already running.
Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_write_f.whenToChange: Add a destination before asking an agent to export outside your project folder, or to export an unsaved project. Remove folders when access is no longer needed.

Agents/Updates/check_updates.summary: Check once at startup whether a newer build is available.
Agents/Updates/check_updates.description: Suhina asks GitHub about the selected update channel once after starting. A newer build can be offered for you to download; enabling the check does not install or restart anything automatically. Help → Check for updates can still check manually when this is off.

options.name: On
options.description: Make the startup update check. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Skip the automatic startup check; manual checking remains available.

Agents/Updates/check_updates.whenToChange: Turn this off if you prefer to check for updates manually, for example when working offline.

Agents/Updates/update_channel.summary: Choose the builds offered by the update checker.
Agents/Updates/update_channel.description: An update channel chooses which Suhina builds the checker looks for. Nightly builds follow ongoing development. Test builds are produced for proposed changes and appear as a choice only in Developer mode or when Suhina itself is a test build. Without either condition, the effective channel is Nightly. Checking and installation are separate actions.

options.name: Nightly
options.description: Look for the nightly build. This is the default channel.

options.name: Test builds
options.description: List pull-request test builds for your platform when this channel is available. Downloading one requires signing in through the GitHub CLI.

Agents/Updates/update_channel.whenToChange: Use Test builds when testing a particular proposed change, and return to Nightly for the regular development builds.

Agents/Advanced/developer_mode.summary: Expose test builds in the update channel choices.
Agents/Advanced/developer_mode.description: Developer mode makes the Test builds update channel available. It does not select that channel or download a build on its own. Downloading a test build requires the GitHub CLI and an explicit connection from the update dialog. A running test build already exposes Test builds even with Developer mode off.

options.name: On
options.description: Add Test builds to the channel choices.

options.name: Off
options.description: Keep the usual channel choices unless the running app is itself a test build. This is the default.

Agents/Advanced/developer_mode.whenToChange: Enable this when you have been asked to try a test build for a fix or feature.

Plugins/Actions/Plug-in actions.summary: Scan the plug-in folders again or open the plug-in manager.
Plugins/Actions/Plug-in actions.description: Scan checks new or changed plug-in files in the folders that are switched on; Rescan all checks every file again. Manage plug-ins opens a searchable table of found, disabled, failed and incompatible files. The buttons sit above the folder list because they act on it. They do nothing while a scan is already running.

options.name: Scan / Rescan all
options.description: Scan new and changed files, or request a full rescan.

options.name: Manage plug-ins
options.description: Open the catalog, toggle individual plug-ins and use Scan again on a failed or incompatible file.

Plugins/Actions/Plug-in actions.whenToChange: Add a custom installation folder when a plug-in is missing. Use Manage plug-ins to inspect a loading failure or temporarily disable a problematic plug-in.
